finite_only.max_abs_coordinate_rule: reject a decoded coordinate whose absolute value exceeds 8x the maximum absolute coordinate of the clean corpus for that dataset
finite_only.subnormal_policy: allowed; decoded subnormals are recorded as such in the bit manifest

bitflip_policy.reporting: sign, exponent, and mantissa flips are reported separately for fp32 and fp16
bitflip_policy.reversibility: every mutation records original bits, flipped bits, decoded values, and delta_{i,c,l}, and must be exactly reversible

unrestricted_ieee754.description: No value filter. Reported as a separate condition because exponent flips can otherwise dominate every result.

budgets.nesting_rule: b_{i,c,l} <= f_{i,c} <= v_i, with sum v_i <= BV, sum_c f_{i,c} <= BF v_i, and sum b_{i,c,l} <= K
budgets.vector_pool: flips are restricted to the locally exposed pool A = union over Qcal of L(q)

claims.exit_gate: ASR_index above random-flip and matched-budget baselines on Qtest, with a reproducible stale-versus-exact and stale-versus-rebuilt gap.
claims.statement: Under a bit budget K, localized gray-box bit flips cause stale HNSW to miss the clean exact nearest neighbour on held-out queries for which exact search still retains it.
claims.stop_condition: If exact search degrades as much as stale HNSW, report a vector-corruption result, not graph amplification.

claims.exit_gate: Increase in real target visitation above clean, matched-random, and untargeted baselines. A fall in P_hit alone is untargeted disruption, not steering.
claims.statement: The same bit budget can raise the rate at which the real stale-HNSW trace visits a pre-specified wrong node v_tar(q) fixed before bit selection.
claims.stop_condition: If targeted soft-route hits do not move real visitation, the targeted claim is dropped.

claims.exit_gate: Strict ASR_target on pre-registered eligible queries; visitation alone is not sufficient.
claims.statement: For eligible held-out queries, the attack makes stale HNSW return v_tar(q) while exact search still holds i*(q) and does not hold v_tar(q).
claims.stop_condition: If visitation does not convert into final output, report steering without retrieval control.

claims.exit_gate: Increased real work on the exact-retained stratum. A latency claim additionally requires reproducible timing on controlled hardware; a larger J_delay alone is not sufficient.
claims.statement: Bit flips increase the real local search work stale HNSW needs, at fixed efSearch and at matched recall, on the stratum of queries whose exact answer is retained.
claims.stop_condition: If matched-recall work does not increase, no resource-amplification claim is made.

claims.exit_gate: Reproducible stale-index gap against both exact and rebuilt search across datasets, M, efSearch, and numeric types.
claims.statement: Core hypothesis: a stale HNSW graph amplifies sparse stored-vector corruption relative to exact search over the same corrupted vectors and to a graph rebuilt from them.
claims.stop_condition: Absent the gap, the project reports a boundary or negative result.

comparisons.primary_comparison: hnsw_stale against both exact and hnsw_rebuilt over the same corrupted vectors, at matched K, M, efSearch and k, on held-out queries that clean HNSW answered correctly
comparisons.work_metric_note: latency is reported separately from the deterministic counters and never substituted for them

hard case: isotropic high-dimensional geometry with weak cluster structure
norm-spread control: cosine ignores norms, exponent flips do not

loader.checksums: sha256 of both files must be recorded in docs/protocol_changelog.md before first use
sha256 of both files must be recorded in docs/protocol_changelog.md before first use
sha256 of both files must be recorded in docs/protocol_changelog.md before first use

datasets.role: Phase 8 RAG-like retrieval setting; blocked until the model revision is pinned

embedding_models.description: Raw feature vectors (synthetic corpora and SIFT descriptors); no embedding model in the loop.

embedding_models.pin_note: The model revision hash must be pinned by a new protocol version before any external-data run. Until then no claim may cite this model.

hnsw.entry_point_rule: the highest-level element, as in Algorithm 5; the attacker may not change it
hnsw.insertion_order: identity order of element ids, fixed by the corpus construction

leakage_policy.enforcement: braid.splits seals held-out query ids at runtime; every unseal attempt, permitted or refused, is written to results/audit/leakage_audit.jsonl and read by the Phase 0 gate.
leakage_policy.rule: Bit sets, target rules, eligibility rules, surrogate parameters (gamma, H, tau, lambda, cost weights), efSearch grids, and success thresholds are chosen on Qcal only.

notes: This file is the Phase 0 freeze. Every value here must be fixed before any attack bit is
selected. Editing a frozen file breaks its content hash on load; changes require a new
versioned protocol file plus an entry in docs/protocol_changelog.md.

dev.description: Development subset: both synthetic geometries, two M values, three efSearch values, 200 calibration queries.

full.description: The frozen grid in full. The only profile whose results may support a claim.

smoke.description: Pipeline check, minutes not hours. Exercises every Phase 1 instrument on one small corpus.

seeds.note: All randomness is label-addressed, so no run depends on stored state beyond this root seed.

splits.policy: uniform random permutation of query ids under the 'split/<dataset_id>' stream; the first half is Qcal, the rest is Qtest
splits.test_split_use: held-out evaluation only, in phases listed under leakage_policy.test_unseal_allowed_phases

surrogate.H_note: H counts surrogate transitions and is swept independently of efSearch, which controls real candidate-search breadth.
surrogate.validation_gate: Phase 4: the surrogate must predict real stale-HNSW next-node choices better than random ranking on a calibration-only validation split, or route objectives are reported as search heuristics only.

distance.storage_note: Bit flips target raw stored coordinates. A deployment that stores pre-normalized vectors is a separate condition and must be reported separately.

known_divergences: space='cosine' normalizes stored copies at insert time, which moves the attack surface off raw stored coordinates; parity runs therefore pre-normalize and use space='ip'
BFIndex(space='cosine') does not normalize at all in 0.8.0
no API exposes visited sets, candidate expansions, or neighbour lists, which is why the primary implementation is the instrumented one
cross_check.name: hnswlib
cross_check.role: recall-parity and graph-statistics cross-check; the deployed implementation any external claim must be reproduced on

primary.algorithm_source: Malkov & Yashunin 2020, Algorithms 1-5, with hnswlib defaults (max_M0 = 2M, extendCandidates = false, keepPrunedConnections = true)
primary.name: braid.hnsw.reference
primary.role: instrumented reference implementation used for all objective optimization and trace extraction

eligibility.note: Reachability is checked before optimization and its coverage reported; it is never applied as a post hoc query filter.

targets.lambda_note: lambda = 0 is the pure targeted-likelihood objective; any lambda > 0 run must be pre-registered here before use.

rules.description: One node for all queries: the element of A with the highest visit count across the Qcal local traces, ties broken by smallest element id. Fixed across Qcal and Qtest.
rules.information_used: calibration-trace visit counts only, which the gray-box model already exposes

rules.description: Per query: among elements of A that are reachable from u0(q) within H steps under the clean local topology and are not i*(q), the one with the largest clean distance rank, ties broken by smallest element id.
rules.information_used: clean local trace, local neighbour lists, and clean local distances

rules.description: Per query: the element of L(q) other than i*(q) with the largest exposed local degree, ties broken by smallest element id. Calibration diagnostic only.
